description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.

- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

The closest match, #172 (closed), is the data-loss bug these tests would guard — related context, not a duplicate. **Correction to the premise:** the issue states only `decode_seed` and `parse_and_render` are covered, but PR #239 (commit `995e5ee`, merged today) already added substantial `cmd_apply` coverage on main: - `tests/test_cli_apply.py` — re-apply preserves content above/below the `:root` block (the `_merge_theme_css` behavior from #192/#172), idempotence of a second `apply`, preset switching, and end-to-end wiring through the argparse entry point. - `tests/test_cli_theme_css.py` — `cmd_apply` writes the radius scale without duplicating it on re-apply, and `cmd_init()` + `apply` interplay preserves the shimmer/scrollbar `@theme inline` blocks. So two of the four suggested cases ("apply `--preset b0` … run twice" and "CSS merge preserves content before `:root`") are already satisfied; worth updating the body. **Remaining gap and plan:** `patch_rxconfig` (`cli/main.py:344`) still has zero direct tests — no test file imports it. Concrete plan: 1. New `tests/test_cli_patch_rxconfig.py`, following the fixture pattern already in `test_cli_apply.py` (`tmp_path` project root, write `rxconfig.py`, `monkeypatch.chdir`; no `conftest.py`, per repo convention). 2. Cases to cover: - **Fresh config:** `config = rx.Config(app_name=...)` gains a `plugins=[TailwindV4Plugin(...)]` entry plus the prepended `from reflex.plugins.shared_tailwind import TailwindConfig` import; assert the result still parses via `ast.parse`. - **Idempotence:** a second `cmd_init()` leaves `rxconfig.py` byte-identical (early return on `var(--background)`). - **AST variants:** a config that already has `plugins=[…]` merges without duplication and strips a stale `rx.plugins.TailwindV4Plugin()`; the `_append_plugins_fallback` path for content the AST pass can't patch. - **Warning path:** content with no `rx.Config(`/`rx.config(` → file untouched, warning printed (assert via `capsys`). - **Command-level guard:** `cmd_init` without `rxconfig.py` exits 1 (`pytest.raises(SystemExit)`). Note a *missing* file is not an early return inside `patch_rxconfig` itself — `read_text()` raises before the `try`, so the "missing config" case in the issue belongs at the `cmd_init` level, which already guards it. 3. Runs under the standard `uv run pytest tests/ -q` gate; no runtime code changes, matching the issue's acceptance criteria.   ｜ [Implement a fix ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/246?action=build) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/actions/runs/41526031862/job/125553886633) ｜ via [Pullfrog](https://pullfrog.com) ｜ Using `glm-5p3-flash` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai) --

# noqa: INP001
"""Regression coverage for ``buridan apply`` (``cmd_apply``) theme rewriting.

The replace path — re-applying a preset over a file that already contains a
``:root {`` / ``.dark {`` theme block — must preserve the *entire* surrounding
file: content above the theme block, the freshly generated theme block, and
content below the theme block. Re-applying a preset to switch themes is the
documented workflow surfaced by https://buridan-ui.com/create (see
``cli/README.md`` and ``app/templates/compiler.py``, which emits
``uv run buridan apply --preset {seed}`` into generated project templates).

Git blame traces the original data-loss bug to commit ``8dc954c`` which added
``cmd_apply``: on re-apply it rebuilt the file as ``theme_css + after`` and
silently dropped ``lines[:start_line]`` — every ``@import``/``@tailwind``
directive and hand-written rule sitting above the theme block was destroyed.
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cli.main import CHARS, cmd_apply, generate_theme_css, main

# ── valid preset seeds ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _to_base62(value: int, width: int) -> str:
    """Encode an integer using the seed codec's fixed-width base-62 alphabet."""
    out = ""
    for _ in range(width):
        out += CHARS[value % 62]
        value //= 62
    return out


def _seed_for_number(number: int) -> str:
    """Encode a packed config number into a valid 9-char preset seed."""
    checksum = (number * 12345) % 916132832
    return _to_base62(number, 4) + _to_base62(checksum, 5)


_PRESET_A = "b0"
_PRESET_B = _seed_for_number(0)
_THEME_A = generate_theme_css(_PRESET_A)
_THEME_B = generate_theme_css(_PRESET_B)

# A custom placeholder theme distinct from any generated preset. Used to detect
# whether ``cmd_apply`` actually REPLACES the block (not merely appends to it):
# the ``--marker`` declarations must disappear after a real apply.
_CUSTOM_THEME = (
    ":root {\n"
    "    --marker: light-sentinel;\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    ".dark {\n"
    "    --marker: dark-sentinel;\n"
    "}"
)

# Content a user keeps above the theme block (font imports, Tailwind v4
# directives, hand-written rules). No trailing newline — keeps ``before`` an
# identity after ``"\n".join(lines[:start_line]).rstrip("\n")``.
_PREFIX = (
    '@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter");\n'
    "@tailwind base;\n"
    "@tailwind components;\n"
    "@tailwind utilities;\n"
    "\n"
    "/* custom user variables kept outside the theme block */\n"
    "::selection {\n"
    "    background: var(--foreground);\n"
    "    color: var(--background);\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    "body {\n"
    "    background-color: var(--background);\n"
    "}"
)

# Content a user keeps below the theme block (utility classes appended by init
# or hand-written). No leading newline — keeps ``after`` an identity after
# ``"\n".join(lines[end_line + 1:]).lstrip("\n")``.
_SUFFIX = (
    "/* user utility blocks appended after the theme */\n"
    ".my-card {\n"
    "    border-radius: var(--radius);\n"
    "    padding: var(--card-padding);\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    ".hidden-thing {\n"
    "    display: none;\n"
    "}"
)


# ── fixtures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.fixture
def reflex_project(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    """Create a minimal Reflex project root in a temp dir and chdir into it."""
    (tmp_path / "rxconfig.py").write_text("import reflex as rx\nconfig = rx.Config()\n")
    (tmp_path / "assets").mkdir()
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


def _globals(root: Path) -> Path:
    return root / "assets" / "globals.css"


def _write_globals(root: Path, content: str) -> None:
    _globals(root).write_text(content)


def _read_globals(root: Path) -> str:
    return _globals(root).read_text()


# ── tests: re-apply preserves surrounding content (the bug) ────────────────────


def test_reapply_preserves_content_above_and_below_root_block(
    reflex_project: Path,
) -> None:
    """Re-applying over a full file (prefix + theme + suffix) preserves the
    prefix and suffix while replacing the theme — no silent data loss.
    """
    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    result = _read_globals(reflex_project)

    assert result == _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _THEME_A + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX + "\n"
    assert "--marker" not in result
    assert result.count(":root {") == 1
    assert result.count(".dark {") == 1
    assert result.index("@tailwind base;") < result.index(":root {")
    assert result.index(":root {") < result.index(".my-card {")


def test_reapply_is_idempotent(reflex_project: Path) -> None:
    """Applying the same preset twice yields a stable file (no duplication of
    the theme block, no erosion of surrounding content).
    """
    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    first = _read_globals(reflex_project)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    second = _read_globals(reflex_project)
    assert second == first
    assert second.count(":root {") == 1
    assert second.count(".dark {") == 1
    assert "@tailwind base;" in second
    assert ".my-card {" in second


def test_reapply_switching_presets_preserves_surrounding_content(
    reflex_project: Path,
) -> None:
    """Switching presets via re-apply keeps the prefix and suffix and lands on
    the new theme block (the documented workflow from the theme builder).
    """
    assert _THEME_A != _THEME_B, "test presets must produce different themes"

    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_B)
    result = _read_globals(reflex_project)

    assert result == _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _THEME_B + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX + "\n"
    assert result.count(":root {") == 1
    assert result.count(".dark {") == 1
    assert "--marker" not in result
    assert "@tailwind base;" in result
    assert ".my-card {" in result


def test_apply_via_cli_entry_point_preserves_prefix(
    reflex_project: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """End-to-end through the argparse entry point: ``buridan apply --preset``
    must route through cmd_apply and preserve the prefix (no wiring bypass).
    """
    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["buridan", "apply", "--preset", _PRESET_A])
    main()
    result = _read_globals(reflex_project)
    assert result == _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _THEME_A + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX + "\n"
    assert "--marker" not in result

# noqa: INP001
"""Regression coverage for ``buridan apply`` (``cmd_apply``) theme rewriting.

The replace path — re-applying a preset over a file that already contains a
``:root {`` / ``.dark {`` theme block — must preserve the *entire* surrounding
file: content above the theme block, the freshly generated theme block, and
content below the theme block. Re-applying a preset to switch themes is the
documented workflow surfaced by https://buridan-ui.com/create (see
``cli/README.md`` and ``app/templates/compiler.py``, which emits
``uv run buridan apply --preset {seed}`` into generated project templates).

Git blame traces the original data-loss bug to commit ``8dc954c`` which added
``cmd_apply``: on re-apply it rebuilt the file as ``theme_css + after`` and
silently dropped ``lines[:start_line]`` — every ``@import``/``@tailwind``
directive and hand-written rule sitting above the theme block was destroyed.
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cli.main import CHARS, cmd_apply, generate_theme_css, main

# ── valid preset seeds ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _to_base62(value: int, width: int) -> str:
    """Encode an integer using the seed codec's fixed-width base-62 alphabet."""
    out = ""
    for _ in range(width):
        out += CHARS[value % 62]
        value //= 62
    return out


def _seed_for_number(number: int) -> str:
    """Encode a packed config number into a valid 9-char preset seed."""
    checksum = (number * 12345) % 916132832
    return _to_base62(number, 4) + _to_base62(checksum, 5)


_PRESET_A = "b0"
_PRESET_B = _seed_for_number(0)
_THEME_A = generate_theme_css(_PRESET_A)
_THEME_B = generate_theme_css(_PRESET_B)

# A custom placeholder theme distinct from any generated preset. Used to detect
# whether ``cmd_apply`` actually REPLACES the block (not merely appends to it):
# the ``--marker`` declarations must disappear after a real apply.
_CUSTOM_THEME = (
    ":root {\n"
    "    --marker: light-sentinel;\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    ".dark {\n"
    "    --marker: dark-sentinel;\n"
    "}"
)

# Content a user keeps above the theme block (font imports, Tailwind v4
# directives, hand-written rules). No trailing newline — keeps ``before`` an
# identity after ``"\n".join(lines[:start_line]).rstrip("\n")``.
_PREFIX = (
    '@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter");\n'
    "@tailwind base;\n"
    "@tailwind components;\n"
    "@tailwind utilities;\n"
    "\n"
    "/* custom user variables kept outside the theme block */\n"
    "::selection {\n"
    "    background: var(--foreground);\n"
    "    color: var(--background);\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    "body {\n"
    "    background-color: var(--background);\n"
    "}"
)

# Content a user keeps below the theme block (utility classes appended by init
# or hand-written). No leading newline — keeps ``after`` an identity after
# ``"\n".join(lines[end_line + 1:]).lstrip("\n")``.
_SUFFIX = (
    "/* user utility blocks appended after the theme */\n"
    ".my-card {\n"
    "    border-radius: var(--radius);\n"
    "    padding: var(--card-padding);\n"
    "}\n"
    "\n"
    ".hidden-thing {\n"
    "    display: none;\n"
    "}"
)


# ── fixtures ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


@pytest.fixture
def reflex_project(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    """Create a minimal Reflex project root in a temp dir and chdir into it."""
    (tmp_path / "rxconfig.py").write_text("import reflex as rx\nconfig = rx.Config()\n")
    (tmp_path / "assets").mkdir()
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


def _globals(root: Path) -> Path:
    return root / "assets" / "globals.css"


def _write_globals(root: Path, content: str) -> None:
    _globals(root).write_text(content)


def _read_globals(root: Path) -> str:
    return _globals(root).read_text()


# ── tests: re-apply preserves surrounding content (the bug) ────────────────────


def test_reapply_preserves_content_above_and_below_root_block(
    reflex_project: Path,
) -> None:
    """Re-applying over a full file (prefix + theme + suffix) preserves the
    prefix and suffix while replacing the theme — no silent data loss.
    """
    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    result = _read_globals(reflex_project)

    assert result == _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _THEME_A + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX + "\n"
    assert "--marker" not in result
    assert result.count(":root {") == 1
    assert result.count(".dark {") == 1
    assert result.index("@tailwind base;") < result.index(":root {")
    assert result.index(":root {") < result.index(".my-card {")


def test_reapply_is_idempotent(reflex_project: Path) -> None:
    """Applying the same preset twice yields a stable file (no duplication of
    the theme block, no erosion of surrounding content).
    """
    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    first = _read_globals(reflex_project)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    second = _read_globals(reflex_project)
    assert second == first
    assert second.count(":root {") == 1
    assert second.count(".dark {") == 1
    assert "@tailwind base;" in second
    assert ".my-card {" in second


def test_reapply_switching_presets_preserves_surrounding_content(
    reflex_project: Path,
) -> None:
    """Switching presets via re-apply keeps the prefix and suffix and lands on
    the new theme block (the documented workflow from the theme builder).
    """
    assert _THEME_A != _THEME_B, "test presets must produce different themes"

    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_A)
    cmd_apply(_PRESET_B)
    result = _read_globals(reflex_project)

    assert result == _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _THEME_B + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX + "\n"
    assert result.count(":root {") == 1
    assert result.count(".dark {") == 1
    assert "--marker" not in result
    assert "@tailwind base;" in result
    assert ".my-card {" in result


def test_apply_via_cli_entry_point_preserves_prefix(
    reflex_project: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """End-to-end through the argparse entry point: ``buridan apply --preset``
    must route through cmd_apply and preserve the prefix (no wiring bypass).
    """
    _write_globals(reflex_project, _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _CUSTOM_THEME + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "argv", ["buridan", "apply", "--preset", _PRESET_A])
    main()
    result = _read_globals(reflex_project)
    assert result == _PREFIX + "\n\n" + _THEME_A + "\n\n" + _SUFFIX + "\n"
    assert "--marker" not in result

"""Regression coverage for CLI-generated theme CSS radius variables.

The CLI injects a Tailwind ``borderRadius`` config mapping
``rounded-sm``..``rounded-4xl`` to ``var(--radius-sm)``..``var(--radius-4xl)``,
so ``generate_theme_css()`` must emit a derived ``@theme inline`` radius scale
defining those variables from the base ``--radius``. Without it, every
``buridan init`` + ``buridan apply`` project silently renders ``rounded-*``
utilities with square corners (Tailwind v4 compiles without warnings).

These tests pin the invariants that are easy to silently regress:
- the radius scale block is emitted exactly once by ``generate_theme_css``,
- it stays byte-equivalent to the repo's hand-authored ``assets/globals.css``,
- ``cmd_apply`` writes it to ``assets/globals.css`` and does not duplicate it
  on re-apply,
- ``cmd_apply`` leaves the shimmer/scrollbar utility ``@theme inline`` blocks
  added by ``cmd_init`` untouched.
"""  # noqa: INP001

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cli.main import RADIUS_SCALE_BLOCK, cmd_apply, cmd_init, generate_theme_css

ROOT_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent
REPO_GLOBALS_CSS = ROOT_DIR / "assets" / "globals.css"

EXPECTED_RADIUS_VARS = {
    "--radius-sm": "calc(var(--radius) * 0.6)",
    "--radius-md": "calc(var(--radius) * 0.8)",
    "--radius-lg": "var(--radius)",
    "--radius-xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 1.4)",
    "--radius-2xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 1.8)",
    "--radius-3xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 2.2)",
    "--radius-4xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 2.6)",
}


@pytest.fixture
def project_dir(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    """A minimal Reflex project root with an rxconfig.py."""
    (tmp_path / "rxconfig.py").write_text(
        'import reflex as rx\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("var", "value"), sorted(EXPECTED_RADIUS_VARS.items()))
def test_generate_theme_css_emits_each_derived_radius(var: str, value: str) -> None:
    css = generate_theme_css("b0")
    assert f"{var}: {value};" in css, f"missing derived radius var {var}"


def test_generate_theme_css_emits_root_and_dark_blocks_unchanged() -> None:
    """The fix must not disturb the existing :root / .dark block shape, and
    the base --radius must still be emitted in both.
    """
    css = generate_theme_css("b0")
    assert css.startswith(":root {")
    assert "\n.dark {" in css
    assert css.count("--radius: 0.625rem;") == 2  # noqa: PLR2004
    assert css.count("@theme inline {") == 1


def test_generate_theme_css_radius_scale_matches_repo_globals_css() -> None:
    """The CLI-emitted radius block must stay byte-equivalent (modulo
    whitespace) to the hand-authored one in assets/globals.css so generated
    projects match the in-repo demo.
    """
    repo_css = REPO_GLOBALS_CSS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r"@theme inline \{[^@]*?--radius-4xl[^\n]*\n\}", repo_css)
    assert m is not None, "repo assets/globals.css no longer has a radius scale block"
    repo_block = m.group(0)

    def norm(s: str) -> str:
        return s.replace(" ", "").replace("\n", "")

    assert norm(RADIUS_SCALE_BLOCK) == norm(repo_block)


def test_cmd_apply_writes_radius_scale_to_globals_css(project_dir: Path) -> None:
    cmd_apply("b0")
    css = (project_dir / "assets" / "globals.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "@theme inline {" in css
    for var, value in EXPECTED_RADIUS_VARS.items():
        assert f"{var}: {value};" in css


def test_cmd_apply_is_idempotent_for_radius_scale(project_dir: Path) -> None:
    cmd_apply("b0")
    cmd_apply("b0")
    css = (project_dir / "assets" / "globals.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert css.count("@theme inline {") == 1
    assert css.count("--radius-sm") == 1
    assert css.count(":root {") == 1
    assert css.count(".dark {") == 1


def test_cmd_apply_preserves_utility_theme_inline_blocks(project_dir: Path) -> None:
    """shimmer/scrollbar utilities define their own @theme inline keyframe
    blocks; cmd_apply must not corrupt or duplicate them, and re-applying a
    preset must not accumulate extra radius blocks alongside them.
    """
    cmd_init()
    after_init = (project_dir / "assets" / "globals.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert after_init.count("@theme inline {") >= 2  # noqa: PLR2004

    cmd_apply("b0")
    after_apply = (project_dir / "assets" / "globals.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert after_apply.count("@theme inline {") == 3  # noqa: PLR2004
    assert after_apply.count("--radius-sm") == 1
    assert "tw-shimmer" in after_apply
    assert "scroll-fade-reveal-t" in after_apply

    cmd_apply("b0")
    after_reapply = (project_dir / "assets" / "globals.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert after_reapply.count("@theme inline {") == 3  # noqa: PLR2004
    assert after_reapply.count("--radius-sm") == 1
    assert "tw-shimmer" in after_reapply
    assert "scroll-fade-reveal-t" in after_reapply

"""Regression coverage for CLI-generated theme CSS radius variables.

The CLI injects a Tailwind ``borderRadius`` config mapping
``rounded-sm``..``rounded-4xl`` to ``var(--radius-sm)``..``var(--radius-4xl)``,
so ``generate_theme_css()`` must emit a derived ``@theme inline`` radius scale
defining those variables from the base ``--radius``. Without it, every
``buridan init`` + ``buridan apply`` project silently renders ``rounded-*``
utilities with square corners (Tailwind v4 compiles without warnings).

These tests pin the invariants that are easy to silently regress:
- the radius scale block is emitted exactly once by ``generate_theme_css``,
- it stays byte-equivalent to the repo's hand-authored ``assets/globals.css``,
- ``cmd_apply`` writes it to ``assets/globals.css`` and does not duplicate it
  on re-apply,
- ``cmd_apply`` leaves the shimmer/scrollbar utility ``@theme inline`` blocks
  added by ``cmd_init`` untouched.
"""  # noqa: INP001

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cli.main import RADIUS_SCALE_BLOCK, cmd_apply, cmd_init, generate_theme_css

ROOT_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent
REPO_GLOBALS_CSS = ROOT_DIR / "assets" / "globals.css"

EXPECTED_RADIUS_VARS = {
    "--radius-sm": "calc(var(--radius) * 0.6)",
    "--radius-md": "calc(var(--radius) * 0.8)",
    "--radius-lg": "var(--radius)",
    "--radius-xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 1.4)",
    "--radius-2xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 1.8)",
    "--radius-3xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 2.2)",
    "--radius-4xl": "calc(var(--radius) * 2.6)",
}


@pytest.fixture
def project_dir(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    """A minimal Reflex project root with an rxconfig.py."""
    (tmp_path / "rxconfig.py").write_text(
        'import reflex as rx\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("var", "value"), sorted(EXPECTED_RADIUS_VARS.items()))
def test_generate_theme_css_emits_each_derived_radius(var: str, value: str) -> None:
    css = generate_theme_css("b0")
    assert f"{var}: {value};" in css, f"missing derived radius var {var}"


def test_generate_theme_css_emits_root_and_dark_blocks_unchanged() -> None:

    the base --radius must still be emitted in both.

name = "buridan-create"
version = "0.1.21"
description = "A command line interface (CLI) for adding components and themes to your project."
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = []

readme = "cli/README.md"
license = "MIT"

authors = [{ name = "LineIndent", email = "line.indent@gmail.com" }]

keywords = [
  "cli",
  "ui",
  "design-system",
  "reflex",
  "components",
  "tailwind",
  "base-ui",

classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",

  "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Code Generators",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/LineIndent/ui"
Repository = "https://github.com/LineIndent/ui"
Issues = "https://github.com/LineIndent/ui/issues"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "reflex==0.10.0",
  "reflex-hosting-cli>=0.1.67",
  "pillow>=12.2.0",
  "PyYAML>=6.0.3",

"""Direct tests for ``patch_rxconfig`` (``cli/main.py``).

``patch_rxconfig`` injects Buridan UI's ``TailwindV4Plugin`` config into a
user's ``rxconfig.py`` via an AST-based pass (``_inject_via_ast``) with a
naive string-replace fallback (``_append_plugins_fallback``). It previously
had no direct tests — only exercised indirectly through ``cmd_init`` — so a
regression in any of the AST branches, the fallback, or the early-return/
warning paths could go unnoticed. See issue #246.
"""  # noqa: INP001

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cli.main import patch_rxconfig


def _write_config(tmp_path: Path, content: str) -> Path:
    path = tmp_path / "rxconfig.py"
    path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    return path


# ── fresh config: no plugins kwarg yet ──────────────────────────────────────


def test_patches_fresh_config_without_plugins_kwarg(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "from reflex.plugins.shared_tailwind import TailwindConfig" in patched
    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(" in patched
    assert "var(--background)" in patched
    ast.parse(patched)


# ── idempotence: a second run is a no-op early return ───────────────────────


def test_second_run_is_idempotent_and_leaves_file_byte_identical(
    tmp_path: Path,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    first = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    patch_rxconfig(path)
    second = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert second == first
    assert "already contains Buridan UI theme tokens" in capsys.readouterr().out


# ── AST pass: existing plugins=[...] list is merged, not replaced ──────────


def test_merges_into_existing_empty_plugins_list(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t", plugins=[])\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(" in patched
    assert "var(--background)" in patched
    ast.parse(patched)


def test_strips_stale_bare_tailwind_plugin_entry(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        "import reflex as rx\n\n"
        'config = rx.Config(app_name="t", plugins=[rx.plugins.TailwindV4Plugin()])\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    # the stale, unconfigured entry is removed in favor of the fully
    # configured TailwindV4Plugin(...) block this function injects.
    assert "rx.plugins.TailwindV4Plugin()" not in patched
    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(\n" in patched
    ast.parse(patched)


# ── fallback path: AST pass can't find a plain `Assign` to rx.Config(...) ──


def test_falls_back_to_string_replace_when_ast_pass_cannot_match(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    # An annotated assignment is an `ast.AnnAssign`, not the `ast.Assign` that
    # `_inject_via_ast` walks for, so it returns None and patch_rxconfig must
    # fall through to `_append_plugins_fallback`'s naive string replace on
    # "rx.Config(".
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig: rx.Config = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "plugins=[" in patched
    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(" in patched
    assert "var(--background)" in patched


# ── warning paths: content left untouched, warning printed ─────────────────


def test_warns_and_leaves_file_untouched_when_no_rx_config_call_present(
    tmp_path: Path,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    original = "x = 1\n"
    path = _write_config(tmp_path, original)

    patch_rxconfig(path)

    assert path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == original
    assert "Could not automatically update rxconfig.py" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_warns_and_leaves_file_untouched_when_config_is_unparseable(
    tmp_path: Path,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    original = "def broken(:\n"
    path = _write_config(tmp_path, original)

    patch_rxconfig(path)

    assert path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == original
    assert "Could not parse rxconfig.py" in capsys.readouterr().out

"""Direct tests for ``patch_rxconfig`` (``cli/main.py``).

``patch_rxconfig`` injects Buridan UI's ``TailwindV4Plugin`` config into a
user's ``rxconfig.py`` via an AST-based pass (``_inject_via_ast``) with a
naive string-replace fallback (``_append_plugins_fallback``). It previously
had no direct tests — only exercised indirectly through ``cmd_init`` — so a
regression in any of the AST branches, the fallback, or the early-return/
warning paths could go unnoticed. See issue #246.
"""  # noqa: INP001

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from cli.main import cmd_init, patch_rxconfig


def _write_config(tmp_path: Path, content: str) -> Path:
    path = tmp_path / "rxconfig.py"
    path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    return path


# ── fresh config: no plugins kwarg yet ──────────────────────────────────────


def test_patches_fresh_config_without_plugins_kwarg(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "from reflex.plugins.shared_tailwind import TailwindConfig" in patched
    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(" in patched
    assert "var(--background)" in patched
    ast.parse(patched)


# ── idempotence: a second run is a no-op early return ───────────────────────


def test_second_run_is_idempotent_and_leaves_file_byte_identical(
    tmp_path: Path,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    first = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    patch_rxconfig(path)
    second = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert second == first
    assert "already contains Buridan UI theme tokens" in capsys.readouterr().out


# ── AST pass: existing plugins=[...] list is merged, not replaced ──────────


def test_merges_into_existing_empty_plugins_list(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig = rx.Config(app_name="t", plugins=[])\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(" in patched
    assert "var(--background)" in patched
    ast.parse(patched)


def test_strips_stale_bare_tailwind_plugin_entry(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        "import reflex as rx\n\n"
        'config = rx.Config(app_name="t", plugins=[rx.plugins.TailwindV4Plugin()])\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    # the stale, unconfigured entry is removed in favor of the fully
    # configured TailwindV4Plugin(...) block this function injects.
    assert "rx.plugins.TailwindV4Plugin()" not in patched
    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(\n" in patched
    ast.parse(patched)


# ── fallback path: AST pass can't find a plain `Assign` to rx.Config(...) ──


def test_falls_back_to_string_replace_when_ast_pass_cannot_match(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    # An annotated assignment is an `ast.AnnAssign`, not the `ast.Assign` that
    # `_inject_via_ast` walks for, so it returns None and patch_rxconfig must
    # fall through to `_append_plugins_fallback`'s naive string replace on
    # "rx.Config(".
    path = _write_config(
        tmp_path,
        'import reflex as rx\n\nconfig: rx.Config = rx.Config(app_name="t")\n',
    )
    patch_rxconfig(path)
    patched = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "plugins=[" in patched
    assert "TailwindV4Plugin(" in patched
    assert "var(--background)" in patched


# ── warning paths: content left untouched, warning printed ─────────────────


def test_warns_and_leaves_file_untouched_when_no_rx_config_call_present(
    tmp_path: Path,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    original = "x = 1\n"
    path = _write_config(tmp_path, original)

    patch_rxconfig(path)

    assert path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == original
    assert "Could not automatically update rxconfig.py" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_warns_and_leaves_file_untouched_when_config_is_unparseable(
    tmp_path: Path,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    original = "def broken(:\n"
    path = _write_config(tmp_path, original)

    patch_rxconfig(path)

    assert path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == original
    assert "Could not parse rxconfig.py" in capsys.readouterr().out


# ── command-level guard: a missing rxconfig.py is caught before patch_rxconfig ──


def test_cmd_init_exits_without_rxconfig_py(
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    # A missing config file is not an early return inside patch_rxconfig
    # itself (config_path.read_text() would raise before its try block) --
    # cmd_init guards against it before patch_rxconfig is ever called.
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cmd_init()

    assert exc_info.value.code == 1
    assert "rxconfig.py not found" in capsys.readouterr().out
    assert not (tmp_path / "assets").exists()
